prompt: The **range** of a data set tells you about the data's…

options.text: spread
centre
shape
trend

feedback.b: The centre is described by the median (or the mean or mode).
feedback.c: The shape is about peaks and tails: symmetrical or skewed.
feedback.d: A trend is the overall direction of a time-series graph.

hints: The range is the highest value take away the lowest value. What does that tell you?
solution: The range measures how far apart the smallest and largest values are, so it tells you about the **spread**.

prompt: Match each word about shape to its meaning.

right.text: Both tails taper off at about the same rate
The tail on the right is longer
The tail on the left is longer
The tallest part of the display

hints: Skew is named after the side with the long tail.
solution: Symmetrical: even tails. Positively skewed: long right tail. Negatively skewed: long left tail. Peak: the tallest part.

prompt: Which of these describes the **centre** of a data set?

options.text: The median
The range
The tails
The title

feedback.b: The range describes spread, not centre.
feedback.c: The tails are part of the shape.
feedback.d: The title tells you what the graph is about, not where its centre is.

hints: Which one is a middle value?
solution: The **median** is the middle value, so it describes the centre of the data.

prompt: In **positively** skewed data, the [[a]] tail is longer. In **negatively** skewed data, the [[b]] tail is longer.
hints: On a number line, positive numbers are to the right.
solution: Positive skew has a long tail on the **right** (towards bigger numbers). Negative skew has a long tail on the **left**.

prompt: Kai looks at a dot plot with its peak on the right and a long tail stretching out to the left. He says, "The peak is on the right, so it's positively skewed." Is he right?

No. Any dot plot with one peak is symmetrical.
Yes. Every dot plot with a peak is positively skewed.

feedback.b: This is a common mix-up. Skew is named after the long tail, not the peak.
feedback.c: A dot plot with one peak can be symmetrical or skewed. Look at the tails.
feedback.d: Dot plots can be symmetrical, positively skewed or negatively skewed.

hints: Is skew named after the peak or after the long tail?
solution: Skew is named after the **long tail**. The long tail is on the left, so the data is **negatively skewed**. Kai has used the peak instead of the tail.

solution: It is called the **trend**. A time-series graph can show an upward trend, a downward trend, or no clear trend.

prompt:
A class grew tomato seedlings in the sun and in the shade. Their heights, in centimetres:

**Sun:** 12, 14, 15, 15, 16, 18, 19

**Shade:** 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 13, 17

Which conclusion is best supported by the data?

options.text: Seedlings in the sun tend to be taller: their median is 15 cm, compared with 12 cm in the shade.
Every seedling in the sun is taller than every seedling in the shade.
Seedlings in the shade tend to be taller, because their range is bigger.
You can't compare the groups, because they have the same number of seedlings.

feedback.b: The groups overlap: one shade seedling is 17 cm, which is taller than some sun seedlings.
feedback.c: The range tells you about spread, not about which group is taller.
feedback.d: Groups of the same size are easy to compare. Use the medians and ranges.

hints: Find the median and the range of each group.
Do the two groups overlap?
solution:
Sun: median 15 cm, range $19 - 12 = 7$ cm. Shade: median 12 cm, range $17 - 8 = 9$ cm.

The sun seedlings have the higher median, so they **tend to** be taller. The groups overlap, so not every sun seedling is taller.

prompt: A data set has a median of 14 and a range of 6. Its smallest value is 11. What is its largest value?
hints: Range = largest value − smallest value.
You don't need the median for this question.
solution:
Range = largest − smallest, so largest = smallest + range.

Largest $= 11 + 6 = 17$

prompt: Two classes did the same test. Both classes have a median score of 15. Class A's scores have a range of 4, and Class B's scores have a range of 15. Which statement is true?

options.text: Class B's scores are much more spread out than Class A's.
Class B scored higher than Class A.
Class A must have an outlier.
The two classes got exactly the same scores.

feedback.b: The medians are the same, so neither class tends to score higher.
feedback.c: A small range means the scores are close together. If anything, an outlier would make the range bigger.
feedback.d: Same median doesn't mean same scores. The ranges are very different.

hints: The median tells you about centre. The range tells you about spread.
solution: The centres are the same (median 15), but Class B's range (15) is much bigger than Class A's (4). So Class B's scores are **much more spread out**: some students did very well and some did poorly. Class A's scores are bunched close together.

prompt: A data set is **positively skewed**: most values are small, with a long tail of bigger values. Which is usually bigger, the mean or the median?

options.text: The mean, because the big values in the tail pull it up
The median, because it is the middle value
They are always equal
The median, because the tail pulls it up

feedback.b: The median stays in the middle of the ordered values, where most of the small values are.
feedback.c: They are only about equal when the data is symmetrical.
feedback.d: The tail hardly moves the median, just like an outlier hardly changes it.

hints: Think about what an outlier does to the mean and the median.
The values in a long tail act a bit like outliers.
solution: The big values in the long right tail pull the **mean** up, in the same way that an outlier does. The median stays among the smaller, more common values. So the mean is usually bigger. For example, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 9 has a median of 2 but a mean of 3.
